results.title: ASEAN leaders maintain Myanmar’s non-political representation until progress on peace plan
results.description: Amid continuing concerns over Myanmar’s political crisis and ongoing armed conflicts, leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) agreed to maintain the country’s non-political representation at ASEAN Summits and Foreign Ministers’ Meetings until there is meaningful progress in implementing the bloc’s Five-Point Consensus (5PC). In a statement adopted at the ASEAN Leaders’ Review and Decision on the Implementation of the Five-Point Consensus in Manila on Nov. 15, the regional leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the peace plan as the main reference for addressing the situation in Myanmar. They also reaffirmed previous ASEAN decisions on Myanmar’s non-political representation at the bloc’s high-level meetings. The leaders pushed to continue upholding the collective ASEAN decisions of the 40th, 41st, 43rd, 44th, 45th, 46th, 47th, and 48th ASEAN Summits regarding Myanmar’s non-political representation at ASEAN Summits and ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meetings "until there is meaningful progress" in the implementation of the 5PC. Myanmar’s participation in other meetings of ASEAN sectoral ministerial bodies or mechanisms, however, “should be unrestricted at all levels,” the leaders said. ‘Insufficient progress’ in Myanmar peace plan The leaders expressed deep concern over the ongoing conflicts and humanitarian situation in Myanmar, as well as the insufficient progress in implementing the Five-Point Consensus. They reiterated their concern over the “insufficient progress in the implementation of the 5PC,” while acknowledging limited progress in humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre). The Five-Point Consensus, adopted in April 2021, remains ASEAN’s framework for addressing the crisis in Myanmar. The leaders reiterated that the 5PC remains the main reference for addressing the political crisis and called for its full implementation to help the people of Myanmar achieve an inclusive and lasting peace. They also called on all parties involved, particularly the armed forces, security forces, and armed groups, to de-escalate violence and stop targeted attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure. “We reiterate our call for the cessation of violence and underscored the importance of a sustained nationwide ceasefire in Myanmar,” the statement said. The leaders stressed that a ceasefire would help create a safe environment for humanitarian assistance and inclusive national dialogue. Calls for expanded humanitarian assistance ASEAN leaders also called for the safe, effective, and transparent delivery of humanitarian assistance to people affected by the ongoing armed conflicts in Myanmar. They urged the AHA Centre to ensure that assistance based on the Joint Needs Assessment directly reaches internally displaced persons (IDPs), while responding to changing humanitarian needs on the ground. The leaders likewise encouraged regional, external, and international partners to increase financial support for sustained humanitarian operations. They called on Myanmar to facilitate humanitarian access and allow the AHA Centre and other humanitarian organizations to expand assistance to underserved communities. The statement also welcomed the AHA Centre ASEAN Monitoring Team Mission to Myanmar on Oct. 28, led by Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro in her capacity as Special Envoy of the ASEAN Chair on Myanmar. The mission marked the beginning of a month-long distribution of humanitarian assistance to more than 11,000 households, including communities in four new priority townships that had not previously been reached by the AHA Centre. ASEAN also welcomed Myanmar’s openness to further expanding humanitarian access to other areas. PH’s special envoy recognized for Myanmar engagements The regional leaders commended the Philippines’ efforts, led by Lazaro, to engage various stakeholders in Myanmar and advance the implementation of the 5PC. They welcomed her visits to Nay Pyi Taw on Jan. 6 and Oct. 29, 2026, as part of her mandate to meet with all parties concerned in Myanmar. They also recognized her efforts to promote inclusive dialogue and engage relevant stakeholders, including regional and international organizations. These engagements included the Myanmar Stakeholders’ Meeting in Tagaytay City, Philippines, from Jan. 19 to 20, and informal meetings with Myanmar ethnic armed organizations and representatives of the National Solidarity and Peacemaking Negotiation Committee in Pattaya, Thailand, on July 13. ASEAN leaders reaffirmed their commitment to helping Myanmar find a peaceful and durable solution to the crisis, emphasizing that the country remains an integral part of the regional bloc. Adoption of ‘calibrated approach’ to Myanmar While maintaining restrictions on Myanmar’s political representation at key ASEAN meetings, the leaders agreed to pursue a calibrated and phased approach based on developments on the ground. “Subject to sustained and concrete progress in the implementation of the 5PC by Myanmar, ASEAN may consider the gradual restoration of Myanmar’s full political representation,” the statement said. They also tasked ASEAN foreign ministers to continue constructive and principled engagement with Myanmar, including through informal discussions consistent with the Five-Point Consensus. The leaders further called for stronger coordination among the previous, current, and incoming ASEAN chairs to ensure policy continuity and sustained implementation of the peace plan. They also acknowledged ongoing discussions to establish a longer-term ASEAN Special Envoy on Myanmar to ensure continuity in the role and to develop ways to assess progress in the country. ASEAN leaders said they would review these decisions at future meetings and tasked foreign ministers to continue monitoring developments and report to the next ASEAN Summit.

results.title: Ducks Activate Ian Moore From Injured Reserve
results.description: Anaheim’s Ian Moore has finally made his season debut tonight against Calgary, as the club shared that he was activated shortly before puck drop. Going down with a lower-body injury back in September, the 24-year-old had been thought to be on the shelf for around 2-4 weeks, but instead he has missed the first 20 games of the campaign.
